name: Western Plaguelands
summary: Toxic mist and undead legions choke the Western Plaguelands, where rival factions fight for ground. Once northern Lordaeron’s breadbasket, its farms and towns fell to Kel'Thuzad’s cauldrons, though life still clings to the soil. The Argent Dawn, Alliance, Forsaken, and Scarlet Crusade wage desperate campaigns across its blighted fields.

sections.title: The Breadbasket of Lordaeron
sections.body: Before the Third War, farms spread east from Tirisfal Glades toward Darrowmere Lake. Hearthglen governed the north from Mardenholde Keep, while Andorhal stored and shipped grain across the kingdom. So Kel'Thuzad made the region his primary target. At Andorhal, the Cult of the Damned put the Plague of Undeath into grain shipments, turning Lordaeron's food supply into its doom.

sections.title: A Land Under Siege
sections.body: The Scourge raised four great plague cauldrons to poison the soil. They stand at Felstone Field, Dalson's Tears, the Writhing Haunt, and Gahrron's Withering. Monstrous Cauldron Lords tend the vats and fill the air with toxic fog. Trees twist with swollen growths, and blighted wildlife rampages through the brush. Beneath Caer Darrow on Darrowmere Lake, Darkmaster Gandling trains necromancers at Scholomance, adding to the undead threat.

sections.title: Divided Factions
sections.body: The Scourge holds much of the region, yet other factions keep footholds. In the north, the Scarlet Crusade controls Hearthglen and purges whatever it deems tainted. Alliance forces gather at Chillwind Camp in the south, while the Forsaken defend their borders from the Bulwark. The neutral Argent Dawn directs the fight against the cauldrons, aids champions of both factions, and guards Uther's Tomb, the region's last truly sanctified ground.

faq.q: Why did the Plague hit this area so hard?
faq.answer: Andorhal shipped grain across northern Lordaeron, making it a target for Kel'Thuzad. The Cult of the Damned put the Plague of Undeath into grain shipments there, then raised plague cauldrons at four major farmsteads to spread undeath through the kingdom's food supply.

faq.q: Who controls Hearthglen in the north?
faq.answer: The Scarlet Crusade controls Hearthglen and Mardenholde Keep. Once a regional administrative hub for Lordaeron, the fortress is now held by zealots who execute outsiders approaching their borders and distrust all non-crusaders.

faq.q: Where can Alliance and Horde players find safe outposts?
faq.answer: The Alliance gathers at Chillwind Camp near the southern border with the Alterac Mountains, where it has a flight master and Argent Dawn allies. The Horde operates from the Bulwark on the western border, reached from Tirisfal Glades.

faq.q: What is the purpose of the plague cauldrons in the fields?
faq.answer: The Cult of the Damned raised plague cauldrons at Felstone Field, Dalson's Tears, the Writhing Haunt, and Gahrron's Withering. They pump plague vapors into the air and soil. Argent Dawn agents recruit adventurers to slay the Cauldron Lords and counter-engineer the toxic brews.

faq.q: What is Scholomance and where is it located?
faq.answer: Scholomance is a subterranean academy of necromancy run by the Scourge and the Cult of the Damned. It lies beneath the ruins of Caer Darrow, an island fortress in the southeastern waters of Darrowmere Lake.

faq.q: Is any part of the Western Plaguelands uncorrupted?
faq.answer: Uther's Tomb on Sorrow Hill, near the zone's southern edge, remains holy and untouched by blight. It is a consecrated memorial to High General Uther the Lightbringer and the lost Order of the Silver Hand.

angles.text: Chillwind Camp is the Alliance's forward garrison. Commander Ashlam Valorfist directs campaigns from there to disrupt the plague cauldrons and avenge Lordaeron's fallen cities.
The Bulwark marks the frontier of Forsaken sovereignty. From there, the Horde pushes east to neutralize Scourge commanders and challenge Scarlet zealots along their vulnerable flank.
As a paladin, you face a solemn trial in Lordaeron's desecrated fields. You can make pilgrimage to Uther's Tomb and fight the horrors of Scholomance and Hearthglen's corrupted zealots.
As a herbalist, you can find rare and dangerous plants such as Plaguebloom and Arthas' Tears rooted among blighted pine groves, where lingering taint lets them grow.
